title: RMIT–ADM+S at the SIGIR 2025 LiveRAG Challenge: G-RAG: Generation-Retrieval-Augmented Generation
extended_summary:
This paper does not report the requested 2025 secondary-education study titled "The role of AI assisted writing feedback in developing secondary students writing skills." Instead, the provided text is a different paper in information retrieval that describes the RMIT–ADM+S team’s winning submission to the SIGIR 2025 LiveRAG Challenge. The paper addresses the problem of improving retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system performance under a shared-task setting where answer generation was standardized, allowing the authors to focus on retrieval, query augmentation, re-ranking, and prompting choices.

The intervention studied is a technical RAG pipeline called G-RAG. Its main components are hypothetical answer generation for query augmentation, hybrid sparse+dense retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion, pointwise LLM-based re-ranking, and prompt-based answer generation using Falcon3-10B-Instruct. The authors also used synthetic question-answer datasets generated with DataMorgana and performed internal system optimization using Grid of Points and N-way ANOVA to compare configurations. Their empirical evaluation is on benchmark questions for an IR challenge, not on students, teachers, or educational writing outcomes.

No school-aged population, classroom implementation, or AI writing-feedback intervention is reported. The context is a research-team evaluation environment using challenge infrastructure, cloud computing resources, and synthetic datasets, with authors based at RMIT University in Melbourne, Australia. The paper’s main conclusion is that the selected G-RAG configuration was effective in the LiveRAG challenge, ultimately ranking first in final manual evaluation. As evidence-based resolution for the retrieval request: the exact target study is not present in the supplied text, and this document should be treated as a false positive or metadata mismatch rather than the sought secondary-student writing-feedback study.
